newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of May 19, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - The race for Java Supremacy has shifted up a gear as Microsoft Corp and Sun Microsystems Inc's JavaSoft Division prepare to release next-generation virtual machines this year, PC Week reported May 19.

Microsoft Corp this week will push Windows NT and BackOffice to their limits with demonstratinos of high-powered hardware, terabyte-size databases and applications running a billion transactions a day, but many IT managers still don't feel NT is ready for the big time as a robust enterprise platform, PC Week reported May 19.

COMPUTERWORLD - Companies looking to offshore programmers to defuse the year 2000 time bombs and develop systems are in for a rude awakening as the pool of available programming talent is drying up, Computerworld reported May 19.

Frustrated users with multimillion dollar enterprise management projects got an apology last week from IBM Corp's Tivoli Systems Inc unit which promised to beef up its customer support amid analysts warnings to clients that its support resources are inadequate, Computerworld reported.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Intel Corp is developing just-in-time compilers to speed up its ability to run Java applications. The strategy aims to help Sun Microsystem's Java move into the mainstream corporate market faster and give Intel an edge in the fast-growing Java market, Computer Reseller News reported in its May 19 issue.

Oracle and CNN plan to sign an agrement on June 4 to create a joint interactive news site in direct competition with Microsoft's MSNBC and Netscape's deal with ABC, sources told Computer Reseller News in its May 19 issue.

INFOWORLD - Next month's PC Expo in New York will feature some of the first NetPC computers built to standards set by Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp, InfoWorld reported in its May 19 issue. The NetPCs are intended as an alternative to the network computer promoted by Oracle Corp and others.

International Business Machines Corp's Lotus unit is preparing a final version of Notes version 4.6 to compete with Microsoft Outlook and Netscape Communications Corp's Communicator, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - For Microsoft, May 20 is the day the company hopes to prove that Windows NT is scalable enough to take on the toughest of enterprise computing challenges but some corporate customers are already putting the operating system through the paces, InfoWeek reported May 19.

International Business Machines Corp is expected to unveil its G4 mainframe line on June 10, Information Week reported May 19, a machine that will feature up to 10 processors. The G4 is expected to begin shipping June 25.

EE TIMES - Trident Microsystems Inc intends to build one of the first commercial graphics accelerators using Microsoft Corp's Talisman technology, in hopes of propelling itself to the forefront of the market for 3D graphics for the PC, EE Times reported May 19.

Chip makers Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, NEC Corp, Texas Instruments Inc, Fujitsu Ltd and Hyundai Group's electronics unit are set to make 128 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, even though the industry had previously decided to jump straight from 64 megabit to 256 megabit DRAM production, EE Times reported May 19.

MACWEEK - Although Apple Computer Inc's Rhapsody Yellow Box took center stage at the Apple Worldwide Developers Conference last week, Apple stressed the Mac operating system and Rhapsody will coexist for years, MacWeek reported May 19.

Apple clarified its operating system strategy last week and many attendees said they had not anticipated Apple's demonstrative commitment to the Mac OS and the cross-platform strategy that hinges on the Yellow Box, MacWeek reported.
